requirement:
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
rationale:
## Verdict
The sources satisfy `requirements.authoring.usage_storage`. The implementation covers each obligation and the tests exercise the main outcomes and failure modes. I found no unmarked implementing code. The points below are minor observations, not gaps.

## Implementation
- **Location and file name.** `UsageLog::start` (`src/authoring/usage.rs`) creates `<state>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json`. It uses `create_new`, and the run ID combines nanosecond time, process ID and an atomic sequence number.
- **State root.** `usage_state_root` (`src/authoring/mod.rs`) takes the root from `config::state_root()`, which the state_location requirement covers. It creates the directory and reports a failure before any model request, so it never claims history was recorded.
- **Outside the project.** `usage_state_root` rejects a state root inside the canonical project root, resolving symlinks through `resolved_location`. It does this before creating any directory and in both file and stdout modes. All callers use it: `author_evidence_with_options`, `prepare_assessment` and `configured_record`.
- **Required fields.** `UsageRecord` carries these fields:
  - `version` (1), `run_id` and `project_root`.
  - `subject` (full name, taken from the label, including the citation label) and `subject_kind`. `subject_kind` is set in `assess_subject` and `followup_sources`.
  - `backend` and `model`, set in `configured_record` once they are known and left `None` before that.
  - `start_time_ms`, and `end_time_ms` only in `finish`.
  - `outcome`, which starts as `unfinished` and becomes `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`. Interruption maps to `cancelled` in `author_evidence_with_options`, `prepare_assessment`, `failed` and `finish_followup`. A run that never finishes stays `unfinished`.
  - `determination`, set from `Judgment::kind()` (`true`, `false`, `FIXME`) and never holding FIXME entry text.
  - `evidence_output` (`file` or `stdout`) and `evidence_written`.
- **`evidence_written`.** `configured_assessment` sets it only after the file or stdout write succeeds. `PendingAssessment::persisted` sets it after the batch write. A failed write leaves it false while the accepted determination stays recorded.
- **Failure reporting.** `failed`, `persisted` and `author_evidence_with_options` report a failure to write the usage record, including whether evidence was already written.
- **No content stored.** The record holds only counts, sizes, hashes-free metadata and fixed tool names. `tool_name` maps unknown names to `unknown`, so model-supplied text does not leak. Rationale, prompts, responses, source text and FIXME text are never serialised.
- **Follow-up conversations.** `followup_log` and `finish_followup` give each confirmation conversation its own record. Those records carry the subject name with a "(second assessment)" or "(verification)" suffix. That is a small variance from the bare full name, but the confirmation requirement calls for a record per conversation and the name still identifies the subject.

## Tests
- **Unit tests** in `usage.rs`: an initial `unfinished` record with no end time; a cancelled in-flight request; completed and failed outcomes; `evidence_written`, the determination and `end_time_ms` on completion; no leakage of source, requirement text, file or item names, or model-supplied tool names.
- **CLI tests** in `tests/authoring_cli.rs`:
  - `usage_record_identifies_its_run_and_unusable_state_is_reported` checks the file name equals `<run_id>.json`, the version, project root, subject, kind, backend, model, `evidence_output` and times. It also checks that an unusable or undeterminable state location fails with no stdout and no evidence write.
  - `usage_state_inside_the_project_is_refused_before_creating_it` covers file and stdout modes.
  - `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` covers `true`, `false` and FIXME in stdout mode and checks `evidence_output=stdout` and `evidence_written=true`.
  - `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` checks that `#125`, rationale text and secrets are absent from the record.
  - `missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence` and `explicit_untracked_reads_abort_without_another_request_or_evidence_write` check `failed` with `evidence_written=false`.
  - `failed_evidence_write_keeps_the_accepted_judgment_in_usage` checks a failed write keeps the FIXME kind with `evidence_written=false`.
- **Batch tests** in `tests/authoring_batch.rs` check one record per subject, a mix of `completed` and `failed` outcomes, and that every record has an end time.
- **Not tested end to end:** a real Ctrl-C/`cancelled` path, and the follow-up (confirmation) records.

## Conclusion
The implementation is marked on all the code that implements the requirement, with `UsageLog` carrying only a `cite`. Tests cover the main design points and failure cases, so the determination is `true`.

:::{req} state_location
Habeas MUST store persistent per-user activity state under
`$XDG_STATE_HOME/habeas` on Unix when XDG_STATE_HOME is an absolute, nonempty path,
otherwise under `$HOME/.local/state/habeas`. On Windows it MUST use
`%LOCALAPPDATA%/habeas/state`. `HOME` and `LOCALAPPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. Features MUST use a named subdirectory under that
state root and document their record formats and locations.
State MUST persist across invocations and MUST NOT be stored in the project
repository, the configuration file, or a disposable cache directory. Habeas MUST
create the required directories when recording state. If it cannot determine or
write the state location, the operation requiring that state MUST report the
failure and MUST NOT claim that its history was recorded.
